title: Brushing your teeth with braces
what: With braces, food gets stuck more easily, and teeth need more careful cleaning. Here is how to do it at home every day.
why: For everyone who wears braces, from the first day until they come off.
duration: usually 5 to 10 minutes in the morning and evening
tell_doctor: If your gums bleed or hurt
If a bracket came off or the wire pokes you
If white spots appeared on your teeth

prepare.title: Brushes
prepare.text: An orthodontic toothbrush with a notch, and a small interdental brush for the space under the wire.

prepare.title: Floss
prepare.text: Floss with a stiff end, or a water flosser, helps clean between teeth. Your dentist can suggest what to choose.

prepare.title: Toothpaste
prepare.text: Regular fluoride toothpaste, unless your doctor advised another.

steps: Rinse your mouth with water to wash away food
Brush above the brackets with the brush angled down
Then brush below the brackets with the brush angled up
Use an interdental brush under the wire between the brackets
Brush the inside surfaces of your teeth
Clean between your teeth with floss or a water flosser
Check the mirror to see if any food is left
feel: At first it takes a long time, then you get used to it
Gums may bleed a little in the first days, and it goes away with regular cleaning
after: Brush after every meal if you can
Avoid hard and sticky foods: nuts, toffee, chewing gum
Cut hard fruit into small pieces
Professional cleaning at the dentist follows your doctor's schedule
red_flags: A bracket came off or the wire pokes your cheek: book a visit with your doctor

faq.q: Can I use an electric toothbrush?
faq.a: Yes, with a suitable head. Move slowly and carefully.

faq.q: Why do white spots appear on teeth?
faq.a: Most often from poor cleaning around the braces. Tell your doctor as early as possible.

reminders.text: Before bed, brush your teeth with braces: brush, interdental brush, and floss.
